## 5. Example HCL (harness)

`root/audit.tf`

```hcl
# Generated by vault-brownfield-codifier
# Capability: root-config
# Doc ref: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs

resource "vault_audit" "file" {
  type = "file"
  path = "file"

  options = {
    file_path = "/vault/logs/audit.log"
  }
}
```

`root/quotas.tf`

```hcl
# Generated by vault-brownfield-codifier
# Capability: root-config
# Doc ref: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs

resource "vault_quota_rate_limit" "global_rate_limit" {
  name           = "global-rate-limit"
  path           = ""
  rate           = 1000
  interval       = 60
  block_interval = 60
}
```

`root/imports.tf`

```hcl
import {
  to = vault_audit.file
  id = "file"
}

import {
  to = vault_quota_rate_limit.global_rate_limit
  id = "global-rate-limit"
}
```

Root-namespace resources need no `namespace` argument and no provider alias.
`sys_config.tf` and `replication.tf` are not created for the harness.

### Coding standards applied

| # | Standard | Application |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Provenance header | `Capability: root-config` on every `.tf` |
| 2 | Provider pin | `hashicorp/vault ~> 4`, `>= "1.9"`, `skip_child_token = true` |
| 3 | Naming | `global-rate-limit` -> `global_rate_limit`; `file` -> `file` |
| 4 | Namespace targeting | Root: neither alias nor `namespace` argument |
| 5 | Secret guard | No licence text, no tokens, no masked values |
| 6 | Ownership | Only audit, quota, generic-endpoint resources |
| 7 | Import blocks | One per resource in `imports.tf` |
| 8 | Zero-TTL omission | Not applicable (quota `block_interval = 0` is omitted) |
| 9 | Cross-references | None needed in this layer |
| 10 | Empty set | No audit devices -> no `audit.tf`; no quotas -> no `quotas.tf` |
| 11 | Validation | `fmt -check -recursive` and `validate` pass |
